prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of nearly flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, which opened moire quantum matter.

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep B013 as my single-part preferred configuration. My test is whether a simple model with one control parameter made a sharp, surprising and checkable prediction, and whether nature then confirmed it in a way others could reproduce. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives that: the twist angle alone tunes the interlayer coupling to a magic value where the bands flatten and interactions dominate. The 2018 transport experiments found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. Spectroscopy and scanning-probe work from independent groups, and the extension to twisted multilayers and TMD moire systems, show the phenomenon is a platform and not one sample. The discovery that flat bands at a tunable angle host correlated phases does not depend on the pairing mechanism, which is a downstream question. The trio pairs the theory that predicted the effect with the experiment that tested it. B061 is the strongest rival, and my first-round ranking of it sixth was too low. On a second reading, many-atom magic-wavelength interrogation and cross-laboratory comparison at 10^-18 is a distinct, well-controlled result. It remains in my judgement a refinement of a lineage honoured in 2005 and 2012, so I rank it as a safe fallback and not as my first choice.
statement.case_against: The field is under a decade old, sample-to-sample variation from strain and twist-angle disorder is large, and the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved. The record I can reconstruct from memory is also imperfect: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and contemporaneous experimental groups are outside the three-name limit, and earlier continuum-band work on twisted graphene layers (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues) anticipated parts of the picture. If the committee concludes that the priority record cannot be written fairly with these three names, or that the mechanism must be understood first, B013 should wait and B061 is the better choice this year.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B013 but wants to be absolutely sure the credited people did the original work, asks for a historical check on the earlier continuum-band theory, and notes the superconducting mechanism affects interpretation but not the discovery.
responses.response: We agree on the structure of the argument, so I will say what I think the record supports. Earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure work established that interlayer coupling renormalises the Dirac velocity. As I recall it, the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper gave the quantitative continuum model that locates the magic angles and shows the bands flatten there, with interactions then dominating. That is the specific prediction the experiment tested. For the experiment, Jarillo-Herrero led the group that made and measured the devices. Yuan Cao's omission is a cost of the three-name limit that the citation should not hide. I cannot verify the chronology from the files, so I support your request that it be checked before the ballot. I would treat a failed check as grounds to move to B061, not to retitle B013.

responses.point: Kroll holds that the redefinition of the second should not count for timing, that B061 is a distinct achievement because of the magic-wavelength lattice and control of systematics, and calls it an engineering-physics achievement.
responses.response: You have persuaded me on timing. A clock is validated by independent laboratories reproducing and cross-comparing it, and that has happened at 10^-18, so my first-round worry about the pending redefinition was misplaced and I withdraw it as a reason against B061. Your own description, an instrument and not a new phenomenon, is where I still differ. I weigh a new, tunable state of matter and a model that predicted it above a very successful measurement platform, and the 2005 and 2012 prizes already cover neighbouring ground. Your narrow citation for the lattice clock does answer the objection fairly well. That is why I now place B061 first among my alternatives, and I could accept it as the 2026 prize on condition that the B013 attribution check fails.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice is a genuine conceptual step beyond single-ion clocks, that the redefinition is a consequence and not a motivation, and that B008 should not come first because Bohm is deceased and Berry has precursors.
responses.response: I accept both points. On B008 you and others have shown that it is two results bridged by a theme, and Johansson's question about a unified citation does not have a good answer from me. A citation naming a geometric phase as such leaves out Bohm and gives Pancharatnam no credit, so I demote B008 to my second alternative and no longer propose it as a prize part. On B061 I now accept your reading that the many-atom lattice is a real conceptual step. Where we differ is only on ranking: I put the lattice clock as the safer fallback because its record is mature and its credited pair is compact, and B013 first because it concerns new physics with a clean prediction-then-test structure.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B013, lists B019 as an alternative, argues the reproduction across platforms makes the prize defensible before the pairing question closes, and raises the risk of a second condensed-matter prize soon after 2016 and the 2025 circuits prize.
responses.response: I agree that cross-platform reproduction, not the pairing mechanism, carries the case. On proximity to 2016, I do not think it should weigh much: the 2016 prize was for topological phases and phase transitions in matter, while B013 is a tunable correlated platform from a flat-band prediction, and subfield rotation is not a physics argument. I would also add that B019 as a fallback has the worse attribution problem, since the prediction that the HgTe experiment tested came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and is not in the credited trio. So if B013 fails on maturity or attribution, I would move to B061 and not to B019.

responses.point: Johansson asked whether a unified citation for B008 is possible and whether he sees a way to write one, and he stressed the stability criterion of independent laboratories agreeing at 10^-18 for B061.
responses.response: Having tried, I cannot write a unified B008 citation that credits the Aharonov-Bohm result and the Berry phase fairly with only living, named recipients, so I withdraw it as a prize part and keep it only as a lower alternative. I accept your stability criterion, and by that standard B061 is the more secure candidate today. I weigh it differently only in that the criterion also holds for B013 for the central phenomena, since several groups have reproduced the correlated insulators, superconducting domes and flat-band spectroscopy, though sample variability is larger there than for the clocks.

responses.point: Danielsson says an unsettled pairing mechanism and a young field are the strongest argument against B013 and names B061 as the safer choice if the attribution gap in B013 is judged unacceptable.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your fallback. I am answering the chair's question about evidence that would settle it. For me the evidence is not the mechanism but, first, a checked record that the continuum-model prediction preceded and specified the magic angle and that the 2018 experimental credit rests on the Jarillo-Herrero group, and second, continued independent reproduction of the correlated phases, which exists. If the first fails I would move to B061 with you. I do not accept B009 as the safer substitute, because its credit is spread across the founding collaboration and individual source identifications lack second-detector confirmation, as the chair noted.

uncertainties: Whether the historical record supports crediting only MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, given Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure work; I am working from memory and cannot verify the chronology from the provided files.
Whether the committee accepts a prize for a platform under a decade old with an unresolved pairing mechanism, or prefers the more mature B061.
Whether the 4-4 split between B013 and B061 will be resolved by new arguments or by each member's weighting of discovery of new matter against a precision-measurement achievement.
Whether a two-part prize is possible within the three-person limit; B013 uses all three names, so I do not propose one.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate or credited person. I note, as before, that Goran Johansson and Eva Olsson are in the neighbouring Gothenburg physics environment at Chalmers and that the GU and Chalmers departments are closely linked, but I have no collaboration with them or with any credited candidate. My own work on random-matrix theory and statistical physics does not overlap with the shortlisted entries.
